short: The nine human interferon regulatory factors, IRF1 through IRF9, bind DNA with an N-terminal winged helix-turn-helix domain studded with five conserved tryptophans. Each domain reads only a short AANTGAAA half-site, so functional elements are tandem repeats of it: the interferon-stimulated response element (ISRE), written RNGAAANNGAAACT or, on the other strand, AGTTTCNNTTTC. The same half-site also appears in two named composites - the EICE with PU.1 or SPIB, and the AICE with BATF-JUN - which is how IRF4 and IRF8, weak DNA binders on their own, reach their targets. IRFs drive the type I and type II interferon responses, myeloid and lymphoid development, and plasma cell differentiation; IRF6 is the non-immune outlier, acting in epithelium, where mutations cause orofacial clefting.
long:
## The factors

Nine IRF genes exist in humans, IRF1 to IRF9 (an IRF10 is present in birds and fish but not in
mammals). Each encodes an N-terminal DNA-binding domain of roughly 115 residues characterized by a
cluster of five conserved tryptophans - the "tryptophan cluster" that defines the family - folded as
a variant helix-turn-helix. Most members also carry a C-terminal IRF-association domain that
mediates homodimers, IRF-IRF heterodimers, and complexes with non-IRF partners: STAT2 for IRF9,
BATF-JUN for IRF4 and IRF8, PU.1 and SPIB for IRF4 and IRF8. Functionally the family splits along
lines that sequence does not see. IRF1 and IRF2 are broadly expressed and act as an
interferon-inducible activator/repressor pair on the same sites. IRF3 is constitutive and
cytoplasmic until phosphorylated on virus sensing, whereupon it dimerizes and drives type I
interferon genes; IRF7 amplifies that response and is highly expressed in plasmacytoid dendritic
cells. IRF9 is the constitutive DNA-binding subunit of ISGF3. IRF4 and IRF8 are lymphoid and myeloid,
with low intrinsic DNA affinity; IRF5 acts in myeloid cells and B cells. IRF6 is the outlier -
epithelial, expressed in skin and oral periderm, with no established role in interferon signaling.

## The motif

The unit is a short half-site, AANTGAAA, of which only about four bases (the GAAA) are read
strongly. The crystal structure of the IRF1 domain on the PRD I element of the interferon-beta
promoter showed why: the recognition helix lies obliquely in the major groove, contacts a short GAAA
core through three of the five conserved tryptophans, and bends the DNA toward the protein. Because
so little sequence is read per domain, affinity and specificity come from repetition, and the IRF2
structure showed cooperative binding to a tandem GAAA repeat driven by DNA distortion. The canonical
element is therefore the ISRE, written RNGAAANNGAAACT; the data consensus for this family,
CGAAACCGAAACT, is the same element read on the opposite strand, whose reverse complement
AGTTTCGGTTTCG is the familiar AGTTTCNNTTTC form. Two composites reuse the same half-site with a
different partner. The EICE, GGAAGTGAAAC, is a PU.1 or SPIB site fused to an IRF half-site; the
AICE joins an IRF half-site to an AP-1 site, either as AICE1 (TTTCNNNNTGASTCA, four bases of spacer)
or AICE2 (GAAATGASTCA, directly abutting). Paralogue resolution from sequence is close to zero: the
in vitro models for all nine IRFs are near-identical GAAA repeats, and what separates them in vivo is
which partner they cooperate with, not which bases they read.

## Where it acts

ISREs sit predominantly in promoters of interferon-stimulated genes, usually within a few hundred
base pairs of the transcription start site, and in virus-inducible enhancers such as the
interferon-beta enhanceosome, where PRD I and PRD III are IRF elements. In lymphoid and myeloid
cells, IRF4 and IRF8 occupancy is overwhelmingly composite: EICEs at immunoglobulin light-chain
enhancers, where DNA-bound and Ser148-phosphorylated PU.1 raises IRF4 affinity 20- to 40-fold, and
AICEs with BATF-JUN in T cells and dendritic cells. AICE affinity grades the response to signal
strength: high-affinity AICEs remain occupied under weak T-cell receptor stimulation while
low-affinity ones only under strong stimulation. ISGF3, the STAT1-STAT2-IRF9 trimer, accounts for
most ISRE occupancy in a type I interferon response, with the STAT1-STAT2 pair on the 5' GGAA and
IRF9 on the second repeat. IRF6 works instead in epithelial enhancers of the periderm and keratinocyte programs.

## Biology and disease

IRFs are the transcriptional output of innate immune sensing and are also lineage regulators.
Human IRF8 mutations cause dendritic cell immunodeficiency, with biallelic loss abolishing monocytes
and dendritic cells. IRF4 is required for plasma cell
differentiation, and multiple myeloma lines die when IRF4 is depleted whether or not IRF4 itself is
mutated. A common IRF5 haplotype that alters splicing and expression is a reproducible risk factor
for systemic lupus erythematosus. IRF6 mutations cause Van der Woude syndrome (cleft lip or palate
with lower lip pits) and popliteal pterygium syndrome, the clearest case of an IRF acting outside
immunity.

## Reading a hit

A single AANTGAAA half-site is not evidence of anything: with roughly six specified bases it is
expected on the order of a million times per strand in a 3.1-Gb genome. Require the tandem repeat,
or a composite. The most common misreading is confusion with STAT. A STAT homodimer site (GAS) is an
inverted repeat, TTCNNNGAA, with the two half-sites facing each other; an ISRE is a direct repeat,
GAAANNGAAAC, with both half-sites in the same orientation - and its reverse-complement spelling
AGTTTCNNTTTC superficially resembles a GAS. The two families genuinely overlap in biology as well,
because ISGF3 contains STAT1 and STAT2, so ISRE-shaped matrices appear under both labels; one
footprint archetype grouped in this family is named AC0672:IRF/STAT precisely because the clustering
could not separate them. Evidence for this family is comparatively good - most HOCOMOCO models here
carry in vitro HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX support, and most JASPAR profiles here are SELEX-derived - but two
ChIP-derived entries have absorbed a partner's site. HOCOMOCO's ChIP-based IRF8 model
(IRF8.H14CORE.0.P.B, consensus AGDGGAAGTGAAAGT) contains GGAAGTGAAA, an EICE whose 5' half is a PU.1
site, not an IRF site; and one CIS-BP model here (M07978, TGHGGAAATGARTCA) is AICE2-shaped, an IRF
half-site abutting an AP-1 heptamer, and its best match across the databases lies outside the IRF
family. In
myeloid or B-lineage data, check for an adjacent GGAA or TGASTCA before concluding that an IRF acted
alone.
caveats:
A hit identifies an IRF-type element, not an IRF protein: all nine paralogues select
near-identical GAAA repeats in vitro, and their specificity in cells comes from partners (PU.1/SPIB
at an EICE, BATF-JUN at an AICE, STAT2 in ISGF3), not from the bases they read. A lone AANTGAAA
half-site is far too short to be meaningful; insist on a tandem repeat or a composite. Expect
cross-talk with the STAT family in both directions, since ISGF3 contains STAT1 and STAT2 and reads
the ISRE - one footprint archetype here is named IRF/STAT. Most models in this family have in vitro
support, but the ChIP-derived IRF8 model contains an embedded PU.1 half-site and one CIS-BP model in
this family is actually an AICE, half AP-1. Neither should be read as intrinsic IRF specificity.
